short: Money you owe suppliers for goods or services already received.
seoTitle: Accounts Payable — Meaning, Formula and Example
metaDescription: Accounts payable is what a business owes its suppliers for goods and services already received but not yet paid. Part of the free Setu business glossary.
definition: Accounts payable is what a business owes its suppliers for goods and services already received but not yet paid. It is a liability, and in practice it is short-term finance extended by your suppliers.
bodyHtml:
Why Accounts Payable matters

Payables are the cheapest working capital available, and also the easiest relationship to damage. Paying too early wastes cash; paying late without warning costs goodwill and, eventually, terms.

Accounts Payable formula

Days payable outstanding = Accounts payable ÷ Credit purchases × Days in period

Read alongside DSO to see whether suppliers are financing your customers.

How Accounts Payable works in practice

Age payables the way you age receivables, and pay to terms rather than to whoever calls loudest. Where early-payment discounts are offered, compare the discount against the value of holding the cash.

faq.question: Should I always take the early payment discount?
faq.answer: Compare the annualised value of the discount with your cost of cash — often it is worth taking, but not always.

faq.question: What if I cannot pay on time?
faq.answer: Tell the supplier before the due date. Terms survive a warned delay far better than a silent one.
